title: The Army Warranting Program
summary: A warrant is an individual's signatory authority to enter into, obligate funds for, administer, terminate and sign documents under specific appointed or delegated authorities, for FAR-based and non-FAR-based instruments alike. The Army Warranting Program Policy, version 12 of March 2026, sets four warrant classes, a fixed threshold at each class, a rule for calculating the value an instrument counts against your warrant, and a review board that says whether you are ready. VCE-Warrants is the record for all of it.

sections.heading: Who appoints, and the three warrant types
sections.body:
The chain: ASA(ALT) designated procurement authority to DASA(P); DASA(P) may further delegate selection, appointment and termination of contracting officers under RFO FAR 1.403-1(b), and of Grants Officers and Agreements Officers under 32 CFR 21.425; DASA(P) delegates warrant-granting authority to the head of the contracting activity.

For KOs and AOs the HCA may delegate down to a Senior Contracting Official and no lower than the Chief of the Contracting Office; where delegated, 'HCA' in the policy means that delegated official. For Grants Officers the HCA appoints directly and shall not delegate further. At the 411th CSB the SCO chairs the board and makes the appointment in VCE-Warrants.

Three warrant types, three definitions: KO, defined in the FAR and used collectively for procuring, administrative, contingency and termination contracting officers; GO, defined in 2 CFR 1108; AO, defined in 32 CFR 3.4.

One person may hold more than one type, but must meet the qualifications for each. What HCAs may not do is issue the same type twice - a PCO and an ACO warrant to one person - merely to split pre-award and post-award dollar limits. A warrant genuinely limited to an administrative or termination function is still allowed.

sections.heading: Classes, thresholds and calculating instrument value
sections.body:
Policy v12 Table 1 sets four classes and fixed thresholds:

- Class I: SAT, currently $350,000.
- Class II: $500K, $1M, $5M and SaP - simplified procedures for commercial products and services, currently $9,000,000, or $15,000,000 for a contingency, CBRN defense, disaster or emergency operation.
- Class III: $10M, $25M, $50M and $100M.
- Class IV: $250M, $500M and Unlimited.

Warrants are granted at one of those fixed values. Appointing at 'SAT' or 'SaP' rather than a dollar figure means nobody has to be reappointed when the underlying value changes. The threshold applies to everything: FAR-based and non-FAR-based instruments, contracts, delivery and task orders, agreements and modifications.

The calculation rule from paragraph 4.2 is the one boards test. The warrant must be greater than or equal to the cumulative instrument value, and that equals base value plus all options plus any anticipated or actual ceiling plus the absolute value of a modification - regardless of when funds are obligated. Two consequences: a five-year requirement with a modest first year can exceed a Class II warrant on day one, and a deobligating modification still counts at its absolute value. Work the math before you accept the file, not at signature.

sections.heading: The boards: CORB, GORB and AORB
sections.body:
The review board is how the HCA verifies readiness and the strength of a candidate's decision making. There is one per warrant type - the Contracting Officer Review Board, the Grants Officer Review Board and the Agreements Officer Review Board.

Policy v12's general rule: the HCA, or the delegated official, chairs and administers the board and selects three to five additional members with a mix of experience, legal expertise and supervisory backgrounds appropriate to the warrant type. Questions must be commensurate with the warrant threshold, the candidate's role, the organization's mission, the instruments the candidate will sign, and the responsibility to be assumed.

At the 411th CSB, per the July 2026 warrant process workflow: the SCO chairs; voting members come from the SCO, PD, CoCO and/or Division Chiefs and KOs; CONOPS and the Chief, C&P facilitate and do not vote; the board sits the second Wednesday of each month. CONOPS and C&P prepare the questions, cover sheet and scoring sheet, generate the warrant number, and prepare the draft appointment memorandum and certificate for VCE-Warrants. The SCO appoints only on a unanimous recommendation. Confirm current procedures with C&P.

sections.heading: Waivers, legacy warrants and reciprocity
sections.body:
Waivers. The HCA may waive qualification requirements, including the review board, in writing, justified by a risk assessment of the individual's knowledge, skills and abilities with sound rationale and a business case. KO waivers must also comply with 10 U.S.C. 1724(d). Every waiver goes into VCE-Warrants before appointment. The hard limit: the board for an Unlimited warrant cannot be waived. At the 411th a CORB waiver rests on SCO approval, with the memoranda and certificate uploaded in VCE.

Legacy warrants. A person holding a current warrant is not required to be tested, re-boarded or reappointed to keep it, and the exemption extends to increases within the same Table 1 class. To move up a class, the individual takes a new board and is reappointed, completing any qualifications that changed.

Reciprocity. Under ACC Contracting Note 26-03, all ACC SCOs must honor all active and future warrants issued within ACC. Recognition is formal acceptance of an existing warrant's type and value by a different SCO - the individual acts under the recognizing SCO's authority and no new warrant is issued. Warrants from outside ACC are recognized at the SCO's discretion, and a new ACC warrant must still be issued in VCE.

sections.heading: VCE-Warrants: suspension, termination, reinstatement, transfer
sections.body:
VCE-Warrants is the system of record. Every appointment, waiver, suspension, termination and reinstatement is documented and retained there.

Suspension. Reasons in Policy v12 include extended temporary duty, a performance improvement plan, investigation of the holder's actions, and deployment or support to a contingency. It is also the mechanism for a developmental assignment to another organization - and must not be used in lieu of termination.

Termination. Mandatory when the individual leaves employment or moves to a non-acquisition position; also for a change in mission requirements, unsatisfactory performance or misconduct such as Antideficiency Act violations, fraud or negligence, loss of a required clearance, or exceeding delegated authority. Retroactive terminations are prohibited. At the 411th, C&P uploads the termination documents to the VCE record and then terminates; removal from the VCE TDA requires the member's PCF actions to be zero.

Reinstatement. The HCA may reinstate a suspended warrant; a terminated warrant requires a new Certificate of Appointment and letter. Transfer between HCA organizations is not supported by the system, so the original is terminated and a complete new record is built under the gaining SCO. Records are retained six years from suspension or termination unless a longer period is justified in writing.

board_angles.q: What are the four warrant classes and their thresholds?
board_angles.a: Class I at the SAT, currently $350,000; Class II at $500K, $1M, $5M and SaP, currently $9 million; Class III at $10M, $25M, $50M and $100M; Class IV at $250M, $500M and Unlimited.

board_angles.q: How do you calculate the value an instrument counts against your warrant?
board_angles.a: Cumulative instrument value - base plus all options plus any anticipated or actual ceiling plus the absolute value of a modification, regardless of when funds are obligated - and my warrant has to be greater than or equal to that number.

board_angles.q: Your $4M contract needs a modification that pushes cumulative value past your threshold. What do you do?
board_angles.a: I stop, because the threshold covers modifications at absolute value; I prepare the action completely and route it to a contracting officer whose warrant covers the cumulative value, and I tell the customer early rather than at signature.

board_angles.q: Can a warrant board be waived?
board_angles.a: Yes by the HCA in writing, on a documented risk assessment with sound rationale and a business case, with the waiver in VCE-Warrants before appointment and compliance with 10 U.S.C. 1724(d) for KOs - except the board for an Unlimited warrant, which cannot be waived.

board_angles.q: You PCS to another ACC organization. What happens to your warrant?
board_angles.a: Under ACC Contracting Note 26-03 all ACC SCOs must honor active ACC warrants; if I am working under a different SCO the warrant is recognized at its existing value with no new warrant, and on a permanent reassignment the old warrant is terminated and a complete new record is built under the gaining SCO because VCE does not transfer.

board_angles.q: When is a warrant suspended versus terminated?
board_angles.a: Suspension is temporary - extended TDY, a performance improvement plan, an investigation, a deployment, or a developmental assignment - and it must not be used in lieu of termination; termination is mandatory on leaving the position and applies for misconduct, loss of clearance or exceeding authority, and it can never be retroactive.

title: Board Day: How a CORB Works and How to Answer
summary: A warrant board is not a test of memory; it is a panel of people deciding whether they would be comfortable with your signature on a contract they have to defend. At the 411th, the SCO chairs, three to five voting members ask questions calibrated to the class you requested, the Chief of C&P facilitates without voting, and the recommendation has to be unanimous. The way to sound like a contracting officer is to answer in one repeatable structure - State, Cite, Apply, Risk, Route - in forty-five to ninety seconds, and to tell the truth when you do not know.

sections.heading: The 411th board: who is in the room and what happens
sections.body:
From the 411th CSB warrant process workflow of July 2026: the SCO chairs the CORB. Voting members are drawn from the SCO, the PD, the CoCO and/or Division Chiefs, and KOs. CONOPS and the Chief, C&P facilitate and do not vote. The board sits on the Commander's calendar the second Wednesday of each month.

On receipt of the invitation, CONOPS and C&P prepare the CORB questions, the cover sheet and the scoring sheet, generate the warrant number, and prepare the draft appointment memorandum and certificate for upload to VCE-Warrants. The SCO makes the appointment in VCE-Warrants only on a unanimous recommendation from the board members. The SCO may waive the CORB; Army policy does not permit waiving the board for an Unlimited warrant. Urgent applications may run on a shorter timeline based on mission requirements.

Policy v12 adds the general rule: the HCA or the delegated official chairs and administers the board and selects three to five additional members with a mix of experience, legal expertise and supervisory background appropriate to the warrant type. Confirm the current cadence, scoring sheet and routing with C&P before your board.

sections.heading: SCARR: the answer framework
sections.body:
One framework, used out loud, for every scenario question. State, Cite, Apply, Risk, Route.

- STATE the rule in one plain sentence, bottom line first. Not background - the rule.
- CITE the authority in layers: the RFO FAR section, then DFARS or AFARS, then statute or Army policy, then local procedure. Say 'Cite:' out loud; it signals you are done analyzing and are now sourcing.
- APPLY the rule to the facts you were given. Which conditions are met, which are not, what you still need to know. Ask at most one clarifying question rather than assuming a missing fact.
- RISK: name the real exposure - fiscal (Antideficiency Act, purpose, bona fide need), competition, performance, ethics, mission, reputational. Say what would make it worse.
- ROUTE: what you do now, what you can approve at your warrant level, and who must approve or be coordinated with - legal, the competition advocate, C&P, the SCO or HCA, the resource manager, USFK J4 for LCS, FKAQ for SOFA. Close with a one-sentence recommendation.

For a pure knowledge question use the short form - State and Cite, then stop. Do not manufacture a scenario the board did not give you.

sections.heading: Timing, structure and the sound of a good answer
sections.body:
Forty-five to ninety seconds. A clear answer with a recommendation beats a five-minute tour of the FAR, and the board will ask for more if they want more.

Answer the question asked. If it is 'how many days,' say the number first. If it is 'what would you do,' say the action first. Then supply the structure underneath.

Cite in layers and know what layer you are in. Calling an Army policy 'the FAR', citing DFARS for a statutory rule, or presenting a local threshold as if it were regulation are scored as knowledge failures, not slips.

Know the RFO numbers for the top concepts cold: ratification 1.405, COR designation 1.404, only one responsible source 6.103-1, urgency 6.103-2, justification and approval 6.104, commercial simplified procedures 12.201-1, commercial termination 12.304, price analysis 15.404-1, options 17.204-1, rule of two 19.104-1, agency protest 33.104, GAO protest 33.105, final decision 33.205-6, personal services 37.201-2, change orders 43.302, GFP liability 45.104 and 52.245-1, cure and show cause 49.402-3 and 49.607. When a board member uses an old number, answer the concept and offer the new number - politely, once.

Know the thresholds for your class and one above, and know the cumulative instrument value rule.

sections.heading: Saying 'I don't know' correctly
sections.body:
Every candidate hits a question they cannot answer. The board expects it. What they measure is what you do next, because that is what you will do at your desk with nobody watching.

The scoring reality: 'I do not know the section number, but the rule is that the contractor is not liable for loss of Government property unless one of four exceptions applies, and I would confirm the paragraph in Part 45 before I signed anything' scores a 3 or better. A confident wrong answer scores a 1 and colors every answer that follows, because the board now has to discount everything you say.

The formula: say what you know, name where the answer lives, say how you would confirm it, and stop. Do not fill the silence and do not invent a section number - a fabricated cite is the fastest way to lose a board.

Two related moves. If a scenario is missing a fact you actually need, ask for it: 'Is this O&M or LCS funded?' or 'Is this cost-type or fixed-price?' shows judgment. Ask one question, not three. If you realize mid-answer you were wrong, say so and correct it; composure is a scored dimension.

sections.heading: Follow-up probes and what they are testing
sections.body:
Probes follow your answer; they do not open a new topic. The pattern is that a board member takes your answer and changes one fact to see whether you understood the rule or memorized the outcome.

What that looks like: you explain the CICA stay and the probe moves the filing date from day four to day twelve. You explain a set-aside and the probe adds a second interested source. You explain ratification and the probe removes the funds availability.

The right reaction is to re-run the test out loud, not to defend the prior answer: 'That changes it - at day twelve the stay no longer applies, so performance continues and my focus shifts to the agency report.' Boards reward a candidate who visibly re-applies the rule.

Common probes from the board guide: how severability changes your funding answer; what market research must show before you sign a justification and who approves it; whether a contractor e-mail claiming money is a claim; who bears the loss on Government property; who awards an LCS action; what you can sign today and what you push up; and what you say when a Commander names a vendor.

sections.heading: Class-specific expectations and how you are scored
sections.body:
Questions are calibrated to the class you requested, your role and the organization's mission.

- Class I: purpose, time and amount; micro-purchase and GPC limits; simplified and commercial procedures; competition at and below the SAT; the rule of two; price reasonableness; unauthorized commitments; exclusion checks; basic ethics. Mostly knowledge with a short scenario or two.
- Class II: the above plus Part 6 exceptions and justification approval tiers, contract type and risk, options and cumulative value, severable services, ratification, COR designation, personal services limits, agency protests and the KO's role at GAO, cure and show cause, commercial terminations, change orders. At least one judgment question about saying no.
- Class III: source selection and pricing leadership - competitive range, exchanges, debriefings, price and cost analysis, cost realism, certified cost or pricing data, OCI, responsibility, subcontracting plans, claims, terminations, property. Scenarios dominate.
- Class IV: enterprise judgment - strategy, high-dollar approval routing, protests at GAO and the court, large claims, appropriation-level fiscal law, post-Government employment, leading an office. The Unlimited board cannot be waived.

The rubric weights judgment 35 percent, regulatory knowledge 30, composure 20 and communication 15, and the 411th recommendation must be unanimous.

board_angles.q: You do not know the answer. What do you say?

board_angles.q: A board member uses a pre-RFO FAR number. What do you do?
board_angles.a: I answer the concept, then offer the current RFO number once - 'that is the sole-source exception, now at 6.103-1' - and move on without correcting them twice.

board_angles.q: How long should an answer be?
board_angles.a: Forty-five to ninety seconds: bottom line first, then state the rule, cite it, apply it to the facts, name the risk, and say who has to approve - and stop and let them probe.

board_angles.a: Judgment at 35 percent, regulatory knowledge at 30, composure at 20 and communication at 15 - so a candidate who reasons soundly and says they would confirm a number outscores one who recites numbers but cannot decide.
